title: Position statement on antidepressants and depression (PS04/19)
journal: Royal College of Psychiatrists, position statement PS04/19, May 2019
funder: not stated; a position statement of a professional body.
result: Discontinuation should involve tapering that may occur over several months, at a reduction rate tolerable for the patient; withdrawal symptoms are often mild and self-limiting, but for some patients they last much longer and are more severe. The College called for greater recognition in NICE guidelines and patient information of the potential in some people for severe and long-lasting withdrawal symptoms, for NICE to develop evidence-based, pharmacologically informed recommendations on gradual withdrawal, and for support services for people with severe and prolonged withdrawal. It quoted the 2009 NICE guideline that these effects are usually mild and self-limiting over about 1 week, stated that most antidepressant trials were not designed to look carefully at withdrawal and had shorter treatment and follow-up than many patients now receive, and cited Davies and Read: 50.7% in six randomised trials (1465 participants) and 56% across all studies, 46% of these severe, estimates the College described as the subject of much debate.
